solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Funding goal number repulsed banking guys (9)

indicatorNotes.repulsed: driven back, so the number is written backwards
indicatorNotes.banking: holding something as a bank holds money, so the reversed number goes round the guys

blocks.note: an end is an aim or goal

annotation.surface: A fundraising target is pushed back, while the chaps at the bank keep hold of the money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banking' reads as finance, which suits the funding surface; it means holding something inside.
annotation.definitionFit: An endowment is a fund given to support an institution.

entries.clue: Avoid covering publicity stunt (8)

indicatorNotes.covering: one word laid over another, so ESCAPE goes round AD

blocks.note: to escape something is to avoid it

annotation.surface: Someone dodges the press after a publicity stunt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Publicity stunt' reads as one phrase; it splits, with 'publicity' in the wordplay and 'stunt' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an escapade is a reckless adventure, the kind of prank a stunt is.

entries.clue: Pull left, in a manner of speaking (5)

annotation.surface: A figure of speech: pulling left, so to say.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like the usual hedge 'so to speak'; here it is the definition, with 'in' as the join.
annotation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened way of speaking.

entries.clue: Eg Mozart’s piece increasingly hot at every recital venue (7,4)

blocks.note: Mozart wore a powdered wig, a hairpiece
H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A Mozart piece gets ever more heated at each concert.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mozart’s piece' begs to be a composition; it is the wig on his head. WIGMORE HALL is a London concert hall known for chamber music and song recitals.
annotation.definitionFit: Wigmore Hall in London is a leading venue for recitals.

entries.clue: Person itching to remove top employee? (6)

indicatorNotes.to remove top: take off the first letter, the top of a down entry

blocks.note: someone itching for something yearns for it

annotation.surface: Someone longs to get rid of the boss, as a worker might.
annotation.walkthrough: The top reads as the boss or a garment; it is only the Y of YEARNER. The question mark admits an employee is just one kind of earner.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: an employee is one sort of wage earner.

entries.clue: Regulars in Athens unload lots including one mosaic (12)

indicatorNotes.Regulars in: take every other letter of the word that follows
indicatorNotes.including: the phrase for lots takes in the letter for one

blocks.note: to unload goods is to sell them off
a ton = lots, as in 'a ton of work'
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Greek traders sell off auction lots, a mosaic among them.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun; a tessellation is a pattern of tiles fitted together without gaps.
annotation.definitionFit: A mosaic is made by tessellation, tiles fitted edge to edge.

entries.clue: Seize country music composer (7)

blocks.note: to cop is to catch or seize

annotation.surface: A command to grab some country music and its writer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country music' reads as the genre; 'country' belongs to the wordplay and 'music composer' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Aaron Copland wrote Appalachian Spring and other American concert music.

entries.clue: See you online with those posh trousers (3-4)

blocks.note: CU is text shorthand for 'see you'
toffs are posh people, in British slang

annotation.surface: A goodbye message to the smartly-trousered set.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Those posh' stands for a plural noun, the people who are posh.
annotation.definitionFit: Cut-offs are trousers cut short above the knee.

entries.clue: Undesirable child promptly interrupts great rap beat (7,3,5)

indicatorNotes.interrupts: breaks into the middle of the other letters
indicatorNotes.beat: battered into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, split to go round the insert

annotation.surface: A badly behaved kid cuts in on a great rap beat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Undesirable' as a noun means an unwelcome person, which is exactly this Latin phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A persona non grata is an unwelcome person, someone undesirable.

entries.clue: Official capital of Ghana nearly changed (10)

indicatorNotes.nearly: almost all of the word, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Accra is the capital of Ghana

annotation.surface: An official notice that Ghana's capital has almost changed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Official' sits at the front like a description of the capital; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something accredited is officially recognised.

entries.clue: Swimmer — cheat — ultimately dropped back under record (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately dropped: the final letter is left off
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, below the record, so it comes after LP

blocks.note: to do someone is to cheat them
an LP is a long-playing record
hind = back, as in hind legs

annotation.surface: A swimmer caught cheating is dropped to below the record time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as part of 'dropped back'; it is a word of its own, HIND, cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a sea mammal and a strong swimmer.

entries.clue: Feature of ocelot, a long claw (5)

indicatorNotes.Feature of: the answer is featured inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the tail of ocelot, through a, into the front of long

annotation.surface: The wildcat's claw is one of its features.
annotation.walkthrough: An ocelot really has claws, so the surface reads as fact while hiding the answer across three words.
annotation.definitionFit: A talon is a claw, usually of a bird of prey.

entries.clue: Sort dragging wife around grand London landmark (5,6)

indicatorNotes.around: the word for wife goes round the letter for grand

blocks.note: a tower is the sort of vehicle that tows, or drags
a bride is a new wife

annotation.surface: A type hauls his wife round a grand London sight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sort dragging' is read as one idea: the sort of thing that drags is a TOWER.
annotation.definitionFit: Tower Bridge is the famous bascule bridge over the Thames.

entries.clue: Crude hoodlum, but not primarily the boastful kind (9)

indicatorNotes.Crude: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are left in an unrefined jumble
indicatorNotes.not primarily: 'primarily' means first of all, so 'not primarily' takes away the first letter of the word

annotation.surface: A coarse thug, but not quite a braggart.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface says the thug is not the boastful kind; the wordplay says he is.
annotation.definitionFit: A loudmouth brags and talks too much.

entries.clue: Marked unqualified? (7)

blocks.note: reads as 'given a mark' by an examiner; here it means striking, noteworthy
reads as lacking certificates; split the answer into two words meaning lacking ability

annotation.surface: An exam paper marked as failed.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading: NOT ABLE for someone unqualified.
annotation.definitionFit: Marked means conspicuous or noteworthy; split, the answer also reads as not able, i.e. unqualified.

entries.clue: Device powering server (7)

blocks.note: a unit that tops up a phone or battery
reads as a computer; here an old word for a large flat serving dish

annotation.surface: A power unit for a computer server.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Server' reads as a computer; it is the old word for a big plate.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a battery unit and a big platter under a plate.

entries.clue: Burlesque backs away from material? Laughable (7)

indicatorNotes.backs away from: each of the next two words loses its back, its last letter

blocks.note: satin is one material, hence the question mark

annotation.surface: A burlesque performer retreats from the costume material, which is laughable.
annotation.walkthrough: One indicator serves two words: SATIN and RICH both drop their last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Burlesque, as an adjective, means mocking by parody, i.e. satiric.

entries.clue: Spooner’s witnessed instrument case (7)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Rev Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: saw = witnessed; it takes the L sound from the next word
a lute is a stringed instrument; it takes the S sound from the first word

annotation.surface: Spooner saw a musical instrument case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Instrument case' reads as a box for a violin; 'case' alone is the definition, a court case.
annotation.definitionFit: A court case and a suit at law are the same thing, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Gleeful plotters hone manoeuvres to regain control (4,7,8)

indicatorNotes.manoeuvres: moves around, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Delighted conspirators refine their moves to take back power.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a coup; the answer is about composing yourself.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to compose yourself after losing your nerve is to regain control.

entries.clue: Crowd of people flash bishop (3)

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a flash

annotation.surface: A crowd flashes the bishop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like a verb about exposure; it is a noun, a brief moment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for an unruly crowd.

entries.clue: Condemned party brought about protest (6)

indicatorNotes.brought about: turned round, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march

annotation.surface: A banned party led to a protest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brought about' reads as 'caused'; it means turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Condemned and doomed both mean sentenced to a bad end.

entries.clue: Autumn period in Medoc to be relished (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters start after the ME of Medoc and run into the R of relished

annotation.surface: A Bordeaux wine from the Médoc, to be savoured in the autumn.
annotation.walkthrough: The wine-tasting surface fits the harvest month, which is why the hidden answer is easy to read past.
annotation.definitionFit: October is a month of autumn in the northern hemisphere.

entries.clue: Ionised gas, or something in that vein? (6)

blocks.note: the physics term for gas stripped of electrons, the fourth state of matter
reads as 'something of that kind'; literally, the fluid that carries blood cells

annotation.surface: Ionised gas, or something along those lines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In that vein' is an idiom for 'of that kind'; read literally it points to blood.
annotation.definitionFit: One word covers both senses: the physicist's ionised gas and the pale liquid part of blood.

entries.clue: Hotel bath breaking before bathers might use it (5,4)

indicatorNotes.breaking: the bath breaks into the word for before

blocks.note: an inn is a small hotel

annotation.surface: A hotel bath breaks before the guests can bathe in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The bathers are swimmers, who float on a rubber ring, not hotel guests.
annotation.definitionFit: An inner tube is used as a float by bathers at the beach or pool.

entries.clue: For example, gallons the lady will finish (8)

annotation.surface: She'll finish off the gallons, for instance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finish' reads as a verb; it is a noun, a type of paint finish.
annotation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a paint finish with a low sheen.

entries.clue: Really trying to ascend? (8,2)

annotation.surface: A climber is asked if they are really going for the summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Straight up' is British slang for 'honestly'; the second reading is literal, heading vertically.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: in British slang it asks 'really?', and it also literally means vertically.

entries.clue: Lippy trainee not converting powerful diplomat (15)

indicatorNotes.converting: changing the letters into a new form

annotation.surface: A cheeky trainee who does not change into a strong envoy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not' reads as negating 'converting'; it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plenipotentiary is a diplomat with full powers to act for their government.

entries.clue: Obvious things a cabinet must do? (4-3-4)

blocks.note: as in a case so clear-cut it needs no argument
reads as government ministers; here a cupboard with doors

annotation.surface: The obvious jobs for a government cabinet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' reads as ministers; it is a cupboard.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for a clear-cut case, and literally what cupboard doors do.

entries.clue: Mythical hero longs to crush evil (8)

indicatorNotes.to crush: one word squeezes the other inside it

blocks.note: to ache for something is to long for it

annotation.surface: A legendary hero yearns to stamp out wickedness.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface ambition is literally the instruction: the longing word closes round the evil one.
annotation.definitionFit: Achilles is the Greek hero of the Trojan War.

entries.clue: Shudder, blocking out male soprano (6)

indicatorNotes.blocking out: shutting something out, so the letter is removed

annotation.surface: A shudder runs through a young singer who shuts out a man.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Male soprano' reads as a single phrase, a boy singer; 'male' is only the M taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: A choirboy's high voice part is called treble, the soprano line sung by boys.

entries.clue: Fault America where war was fought (6)

blocks.note: a crime is a fault or offence

annotation.surface: America is blamed for the place a war took place.
annotation.walkthrough: The Crimean War of the 1850s is the war in question.
annotation.definitionFit: The Crimean War (1853–56) is named after the Black Sea peninsula where it was fought.

entries.clue: Subversive bachelor sits mid-dance (5)

indicatorNotes.sits mid: sits in the middle of the next word

blocks.note: a reel is a Scottish dance

annotation.surface: A rebellious single man sits out halfway through the dance.
annotation.walkthrough: REEL opens up to take B in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a subversive works to undermine authority, as a rebel does.

entries.clue: Ancient authority’s clothing style (5-3)

indicatorNotes.clothing: dressing round, so the first word goes outside the second

blocks.note: a sage is a wise authority; ’s = is

annotation.surface: An old expert's taste in clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothing style' looks like fashion; 'clothing' is a verb, one word wrapped round the other, and the ’s means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: Stone-age means extremely old-fashioned or ancient.

entries.clue: Audibly try to clear polish out of large rock subgenre (8)

indicatorNotes.Audibly: heard rather than seen, so a word is spelt by its sound
indicatorNotes.out of: the letter for large is taken out

blocks.note: you say 'shoo!' to try to clear animals off
a glaze is a glossy polish

annotation.surface: Someone tries to shift a stain from a big rock.
annotation.walkthrough: Shoegaze is a 1990s British rock style, named for guitarists staring at their effects pedals.
annotation.definitionFit: Shoegaze is a dreamy, heavily distorted subgenre of rock.

entries.clue: Insect queen spinning what’s on its head? (7)

indicatorNotes.spinning: turned round, so the queen is written backwards

annotation.surface: An insect queen turns round, wondering what is on its head.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the insect in the surface: its feeler.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the question mark leans on the insect of the surface, whose feelers sit on its head.

entries.clue: Awkward knight that is adopted by cool group of nuns (12)

indicatorNotes.adopted by: taken in, so the letters go inside the group of nuns

blocks.note: a convent is a community of nuns

annotation.surface: A clumsy knight is taken in by a trendy convent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adopted by' reads as the knight being taken in as a child; it is the insertion, and 'cool' comes before the convent in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something awkward causes trouble or difficulty.

entries.clue: Primate doctor fixed past damage (8)

indicatorNotes.past: coming after, so doctor and fixed follow damage

annotation.surface: A monkey's doctor has repaired old damage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Past' reads as 'previous'; it is a position word, putting MAR first.
annotation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey, a primate.

entries.clue: Work volume, with energy dropping, tries tense medical specialist (11)

indicatorNotes.with energy dropping: the letter for energy is dropped from the next word

blocks.note: a tome is a large book

annotation.surface: Having run out of energy, a writer attempts a tense medical specialty.
annotation.walkthrough: The energy drops from 'tries', not from 'volume', despite the comma after 'dropping'.
annotation.definitionFit: An optometrist examines eyes and prescribes lenses.

entries.clue: Cancel rubbish publication with just one article (8)

indicatorNotes.with just one article: the publication has two As; keep only one

blocks.note: to dis is to rubbish, to disparage
an annual is a yearly book

annotation.surface: Scrap a trashy magazine that has only one feature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' means A, the indefinite article; ANNUAL has two, and one goes.
annotation.definitionFit: An old intensified form of annul; the DIS- adds emphasis rather than reversing the sense.

entries.clue: Tin, perhaps bottle, by the sound of it (5)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: bottle = courage, mettle, in British slang

annotation.surface: A tin can or bottle, judging by the noise it makes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve; 'tin' and 'bottle' look like two containers.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, marked by 'perhaps': tin is one of the metals.

entries.clue: Beer maker runs through mug and pitcher, sat on by bug? (11)

indicatorNotes.runs through: R passes between the two containers
indicatorNotes.sat on by: in a down clue, the bug sits on top

blocks.note: a bug is a hidden microphone, a mic
to mug someone is to rob them
a ewer is a large jug or pitcher

annotation.surface: A brewer's mug and jug get sat on by an insect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mug' and 'pitcher' look like drinking vessels; mug is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: a small independent brewery's owner makes craft beer.

entries.clue: Poorly-voiced complaint? (10)

blocks.note: reads as badly put into words; here voiced by someone who is poorly, British for ill
reads as a grievance; here an ailment

annotation.surface: A grumble that is badly expressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; it is an ailment, and 'poorly' is the British word for ill.
annotation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is an inflamed larynx, which leaves the voice hoarse.

entries.clue: Amid endless work, stir drink (11)

indicatorNotes.endless: with no end, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to till is to work the soil

annotation.surface: Amid all this work, mix yourself a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endless' belongs to 'Amid', not to 'work'; 'stir' is a noun, a fuss.
annotation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium dry sherry.

entries.clue: Pompous old part of speech associated with Liberal individual (9)

blocks.note: a verb is a part of speech

annotation.surface: A grandiose old speech tied to a single Liberal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' reads as a section of an address; it is the grammar term.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: overblown language is inflated and pretentious, pompous.

entries.clue: Benefit wearing a fragrance in teen years (10)

indicatorNotes.wearing: dressed in, so the benefit sits inside the fragrance

blocks.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit

annotation.surface: Wearing perfume paid for with state benefit as a teenager.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Benefit' reads as an advantage; it is the British word for unemployment pay, worn inside the fragrance rather than paying for it.
annotation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective describing someone in their teens, which is exactly this sense.

entries.clue: Burning heap noticed over range (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, turned over, so written upwards

blocks.note: a pyre is a heap of wood for burning

annotation.surface: A bonfire spotted across the cooker range.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' could be a kitchen stove; it is a mountain range.
annotation.definitionFit: The Pyrenees are the mountain range between France and Spain.

entries.clue: Unseemly to take French painter unfinished bread for starters? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.to take: one word takes the other inside it
indicatorNotes.unfinished: not finished, so the painter's name stops short of its last letter

annotation.surface: It is unbecoming to pinch a painting and call it bread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money and 'for starters' means for start-ups; nothing to do with a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Seed money is the funding that starts a new venture.

entries.clue: Short thread on representation that’s needed in IT (7)

indicatorNotes.Short: cut short, losing the last letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the thread sits on top

blocks.note: an icon is a representation or image

annotation.surface: A bit of thread on a picture needed by the IT department.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase standing for a noun: the stuff computer chips are made of.
annotation.definitionFit: Silicon is the material of computer chips, central to IT.

entries.clue: Element turning animated film dark in style? (3-4)

indicatorNotes.turning: turned round, so the film is written backwards

annotation.surface: A cartoon turns dark, lit by a neon sign.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: neo-noir is a modern style of dark crime film.
annotation.definitionFit: Neo-noir films revive the dark, cynical style of film noir.

entries.clue: Salad leaves menu, sparing wings and dip (6)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is plural; endive is a mass noun for the leaves

indicatorNotes.sparing wings: going without its outer letters, its wings

blocks.note: loses M and U, keeping EN
a dive is a dip, a plunge

annotation.surface: Salad drops off the menu, which skips chicken wings and dips.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wings' and 'dip' look like bar food; wings are the outer letters, and dip is a plunge.
annotation.definitionFit: Endive is a bitter leaf used in salads.

entries.clue: Rodents chill behind sleeping quarters (7)

indicatorNotes.behind: coming after, so ICE follows DORM

annotation.surface: Rodents cool off behind the dormitory.
annotation.walkthrough: The dormouse famously hibernates, so the sleeping quarters suit it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the dormouse is a rodent, famous for sleeping.

entries.clue: Internet program with no particular scientific focus (6)

blocks.note: a bot is an automated internet program

annotation.surface: A web program with no particular scientific interest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No particular' reads as 'none'; it is ANY, as in 'any one will do'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: plants are the focus of this branch of science.

entries.clue: Constant pull towards running between golf and church (1-5)

indicatorNotes.running between: placed between the two letters named next

blocks.note: G is golf in the radio alphabet
for = towards, as in 'heading for home'

annotation.surface: A steady tug towards a run between golf and church.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: g is also the physics constant for gravity's pull.
annotation.definitionFit: G-force is the pull of gravity, measured in units of the constant g.

entries.clue: Canine research facility (3)

blocks.note: reads as an adjective; here a dog, short for a retriever breed
the usual clipped form of a scientists' workplace

annotation.surface: A laboratory for dog research.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canine' reads as an adjective; it is a noun, a dog.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are clipped words: one for a Labrador, one for a laboratory.

entries.clue: He got further involved with nascent telepathic ability (7,12)

indicatorNotes.involved: tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone made progress with their budding mind-reading.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two parts of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the old phrase for telepathy, passing thoughts between minds.

entries.clue: Unsophisticated local killing time (5)

indicatorNotes.killing: getting rid of the letter for time

annotation.surface: A simple villager passes the time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Killing time' reads as idling; 'killing' removes T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone unsophisticated lacks worldly experience, which is what naive means.

entries.clue: Sausage about chopped, as far as we can see (7)

indicatorNotes.chopped: cut short, losing the last letter

blocks.clueFragment: as far as we can see
blocks.note: the horizon is as far as we can see

annotation.surface: Sausage chopped up, as far as the eye can tell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like kitchen prep for the sausage; it trims HORIZON.
annotation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a spicy Spanish pork sausage.

entries.clue: Drinking spot on farm peeled citrus fruits when meal should be served (7)

blocks.note: a calf drinks from a teat

annotation.surface: A farm bar serves peeled citrus fruit at dinner time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drinking spot' reads as a pub; on a farm it is where animals suckle.
annotation.definitionFit: Teatime is when the evening meal, tea, is served in Britain.

entries.clue: Leather wear fashioned to keep concealed (7)

indicatorNotes.fashioned: made into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Leather clothing made to hide something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leather wear' reads as one phrase; 'Leather' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: untanned cattle hide is a kind of leather.

entries.clue: Work which may be below an acrobat? (5)

annotation.definition2: which may be below an acrobat?

blocks.note: a musical work for nine players

blocks.clueFragment: which may be below an acrobat?
blocks.note: split into two words, the missing safety net under a daring act

annotation.surface: A job that might sit beneath a trapeze artist.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer as NO NET; the question mark flags the split.
annotation.definitionFit: Musical works are named by their number of players; nine gives this one.

entries.clue: Provide makeover others see in mirror (7)

indicatorNotes.in mirror: seen in a mirror, so written backwards

blocks.note: a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is an English cathedral city

annotation.surface: Makeover clients admire themselves in the mirror.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a bishop's seat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a makeover gives a new style.

entries.clue: Look back into chest, shaking uneasy feeling (3,6)

indicatorNotes.back: turned back, so written in reverse
indicatorNotes.shaking: shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to peer is to look closely

annotation.surface: Peering back into a trunk gives someone a shiver.
annotation.walkthrough: REEP sits between THEC and S.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'it gives me the creeps' describes a shiver of unease.
